sections.greek: Καὶ ταύτην οἱ πολλοὶ μὲν ὡϲ ὄψον ἐϲθίουϲιν, ἰατροὶ δ’ ὡϲ φαρμάκῳ ξηραίνοντι χρῶνται. λέλεκται δὲ περὶ αὐτῆϲ ἤδη μέν τινα κὰν ταῖϲ τῶν φαρμάκων δυνάμεϲι κὰν τῷ πρὸ τοῦδε γράμματι, καὶ νῦν δ’ ἐπὶ κεφαλαίων εἰρήϲεται, τὸν μὲν χυλὸν αὐτῆϲ ἔχειν τι καθαρτικόν, αὐτὸ δὲ τὸ ϲῶμα κατὰ τὸν τοῦ ξηραίνειν λόγον ἐπέχειν μᾶλλον ἢ προτρέπειν εἰϲ ὑποχώρηϲιν. ὅταν μὲν οὖν ἐκκρίνεϲθαι βουλώμεθα τὰ κατὰ τὴν γαϲτέρα, πληϲίον κειμένηϲ τῆϲ κακκάβηϲ, ἐν ἧπερ ἂν ἡψημένη τύχῃ, μετὰ τοῦ ὕδατοϲ ἀναϲπῶνταϲ αὐτὴν εὐθέωϲ ἐμβάλλειν χρὴ τοῖϲ ἀγγείοιϲ, ἐν οἷϲπερ ἐϲκεύαϲται τοὔλαιον ἅμα τῷ γάρῳ. διαφέρει δ’ οὐδὲν οὐδ’ εἰ δι’ ἁλῶν ἀντὶ γάρου λαμβάνοιτο.
sections.english_working_translation: Most people eat this too as a relish, whereas physicians use it as a drying medicine. Some things about it have already been said both in the work on the powers of medicines and in the preceding book; now a summary will be given: its juice has something purgative, but the body itself, in virtue of drying, checks rather than encourages evacuation. Therefore, whenever we wish the contents of the belly to be discharged, with the pot in which it has been boiled close at hand, we should lift it out together with the water and immediately put it into the vessels in which oil with fish sauce has been prepared. Nor does it make any difference if it is taken with salt instead of fish sauce.
sections.translation_status: Own source-side semantic translation; not a target reading or certified modern pharmacology.

sections.greek: ξηρᾶναι δ’ ὑγρὰν γαϲτέρα βουληθέντεϲ, ὅταν ἤδη μετρίωϲ ἡψῆϲθαι δοκῇ, τὸ πρότερον ὕδωρ ἀποχέοντεϲ ἐμβαλοῦμεν εὐθέωϲ ἑτέρῳ θερμῷ κἄπειτα πάλιν ἐν ἐκείνῳ καθεψήϲομεν, ὡϲ τακερὰν γενέϲθαι, μὴ καθέψοντεϲ, ὅταν ὑπαγωγῆϲ ἕνεκα λαμβάνηται. βουλόμεθα γὰρ οὐκ ἀποθέϲθαι πάντα τὸν ἴδιον αὐτῆϲ χυλὸν ἐπὶ τῆϲ τοιαύτηϲ χρείαϲ, ἀλλὰ φυλάττειν ὅϲον οἵόν τε μάλιϲτα. τελέωϲ μὲν οὖν φυλάττειν τὸν ἴδιον χυλὸν οὐδὲν τῶν ἑψομένων δύναται, μᾶλλον δ’ ἀποβάλλει τὰ μέχρι πλείονοϲ ἑψηθέντα.
sections.english_working_translation: But when wishing to dry a moist belly, once it seems moderately boiled, pouring away the former water we shall immediately put it into other hot water and then boil it thoroughly again in that, so that it becomes soft. We do not boil it thoroughly when it is taken for evacuation. For in that use we wish not to lose all its own juice, but to preserve as much as possible. None of the things being boiled can preserve its own juice completely; those boiled for longer lose more.
sections.translation_status: Own source-side semantic translation; not a target reading or certified modern pharmacology.

sections.greek: καὶ μέντοι καὶ φακῆν ἔφαμεν ὁμοίωϲ κράμβη χρῆναι ϲκευάζειν, ἀμφότερα καὶ αὐτὴν ἐργάζεϲθαι δυναμένην, ὑπαγωγήν τε καὶ ϲτάλϲιν γαϲτρόϲ. ὀνομάζεται δ’ ἡ οὕτωϲ ϲκευαϲθεῖϲα δίϲεφθοϲ καὶ κράμβη καὶ φακῆ. καὶ κρόμυον δὲ καὶ πράϲον καὶ πολὺ μᾶλλον ἀμπελόπραϲόν τε καὶ ϲκόροδον, ὅ τι τ’ ἂν ἄλλο βουληθῇϲ ἐπὶ τοὐναντίον ἀποϲτῆϲαι τῆϲ ἀρχαίαϲ φύϲεωϲ, οὕτω ϲκεύαζε μεμνημένοϲ ἐκείνου πρὸ πάντων. ὡϲ οὐ χρὴ ψαύειν οὔτ’ ἀέροϲ οὔθ’ ὕδατοϲ ψυχροῦ τὸ δὶϲ ἑψόμενον· οὐκέτι γὰρ ἀκριβῶϲ γίγνεται τακερόν, οὐδ’ ἂν ἐπὶ πλεῖϲτον ἕψῃϲ, ἀλλὰ χρή, καθάπερ εἶπον ἀρτίωϲ, ἕτοιμον ἔχονταϲ ὕδωρ θερμόν, ἀνελκύϲανταϲ ἐκ τοῦ προτέρου μεταβάλλειν εὐθέωϲ εἰϲ ἐκεῖνο.
sections.english_working_translation: Indeed, we also said that lentil soup should be prepared like cabbage, since it too can bring about both evacuation and checking of the belly. Both cabbage and lentil soup prepared in this way are called twice-boiled. Prepare onion and leek too, and much more wild leek and garlic, and whatever else you wish to change toward the opposite of its original nature, in this way, remembering this above all: the thing being twice boiled must touch neither air nor cold water. For it no longer becomes properly soft, even if you boil it for a very long time. Rather, as I have just said, have hot water ready, draw it from the former water and immediately transfer it into that.
sections.translation_status: Own source-side semantic translation; not a target reading or certified modern pharmacology.

sections.greek: ξηραίνει μὲν οὖν ἀλλήλαιϲ παραπληϲίωϲ φακῆ τε καὶ κράμβη καὶ διὰ τοῦτο τὴν ὄψιν ἀμβλύνει, πλὴν εἰ τύχοι ποθ’ ὑγρότεροϲ ὢν παρὰ φύϲιν ὁ ϲύμπαϲ ὀφθαλμόϲ. ἀλλ’ ἡ μὲν φακῆ τροφὴν οὐκ ὀλίγην δίδωϲι τῷ ϲώματι καὶ ταύτην παχεῖάν τε καὶ μελαγχολικήν, ἡ κράμβη δὲ βραχεῖάν τε τροφὴν ἔχει καὶ ταύτην ὑγροτέραν τῆϲ φακῆϲ, ὡϲ ἂν οὐ ϲτερεὸν οὖϲα ϲιτίον, ἀλλὰ λάχανον. οὐ μὴν εὔχυμόν γ’ ἐϲτὶν ἔδεϲμα κράμβη, καθάπερ ἡ θρῖδαξ, ἀλλὰ καὶ μοχθηρὸν ἔχει καὶ δυϲώδη τὸν χυλόν. ἐπιφανὲϲ δ’ εἰϲ οὔρηϲιν οὔτ’ ἀγαθὸν οὔτε κακὸν ἐξ αὐτῆς ἀποβαῖνον εἰπεῖν ἔχω.
sections.english_working_translation: Lentil soup and cabbage dry in a similar way, and because of this dull the sight, unless the whole eye should happen to be unnaturally moist. But lentil soup gives the body considerable nourishment, and that thick and melancholic, whereas cabbage has little nourishment, and that moister than lentil soup's, since it is not a solid food but a vegetable. Cabbage is not, however, a food with good juice like lettuce: it has a bad and foul-smelling juice. As for urination, I cannot state any manifest good or bad result from it.
sections.translation_status: Own source-side semantic translation; not a target reading or certified modern pharmacology.

sections.greek: τοῦτο τὸ λάχανον οἱ τὴν ἐπίτριπτον ψευδοπαιδείαν ἀϲκοῦντεϲ ὀνομάζειν ἀξιοῦϲι ῥάφανον, ὥϲπερ τοῖϲ πρὸ ἑξακοϲίων ἐτῶν Ἀθηναίοιϲ διαλεγομένων ἡμῶν, ἀλλ’ οὐχὶ τοῖϲ νῦν Ἕλληϲιν, οἷϲ ἅπαϲιν ἔθοϲ ἐϲτὶν ἐπ’ ἄλλου φυτοῦ τὸ τῆϲ ῥαφάνου ὄνομα φέρειν.
sections.english_working_translation: Those who practise tiresome sham learning think fit to call this vegetable rhaphanos, as though we were speaking to Athenians of six hundred years ago rather than to present-day Greeks, all of whom customarily apply the name rhaphanos to another plant.

content_inventory.content: Different human use roles: most eat cabbage as relish; physicians use it as a drying medicine.
Author refers to his work on medicine powers and the preceding book, then announces a summary. These are explicit references, not source-less filler.
Cabbage juice has a purgative component/effect; its body checks evacuation by drying rather than encouraging it.
Under the desire for evacuation, have the original cooking pot nearby.
Lift the cabbage together with water from that pot and transfer it immediately into serving vessels prepared with oil and fish sauce.
Salt may substitute for fish sauce without changing the stated result; oil is not explicitly removed by this substitution.
Under the different desire to dry a moist belly, first reach moderate boiling.
Pour away the former cooking water; immediately place the same cabbage into other hot water.
Boil it again in that replacement water until soft.
For evacuation, by contrast, do not boil it thoroughly: the goal is to retain as much of its own juice as possible, not lose it all.
No boiled item retains its own juice entirely; greater boiling duration entails greater loss. The statement is qualitative, not a measured rate or zero-retention claim.
Lentil soup is explicitly compared with cabbage and said able to cause both evacuation and checking of the belly.
The preparation is named twice-boiled for both cabbage and lentil soup.
The same method is extended to onion, leek, especially wild leek and garlic, and anything else intended to be changed toward the opposite of its original nature.
The twice-boiled item must touch neither air nor cold water.
If the prohibited exposure occurs, it no longer becomes properly soft, even with prolonged boiling.
Repeat the earlier instruction: prepare hot water beforehand, draw the item from the former water and immediately transfer it into that prepared hot water.
Lentil soup and cabbage dry similarly; this is the stated cause of dulled sight.
The sight statement has an exception if the whole eye is abnormally moist; the text does not explicitly assert improved sight in that case.
Lentil soup gives appreciable, thick and melancholic nourishment.
Cabbage gives little nourishment, moister than that of lentil soup; its being a vegetable rather than solid food is the stated explanation.
Unlike lettuce, cabbage does not have good juice; its juice is characterized as bad and foul-smelling.
The author cannot state any manifest benefit or harm for urination: explicit epistemic limitation, not a proven zero effect.
A criticized group calls the same vegetable rhaphanos, imitating ancient Athenian usage.
The six-hundred-years-ago audience is contrasted with present-day Greeks, who use that same name for another, unnamed plant. The whole naming criticism belongs to the entry.

reference_inventory.distinction: The plant/material being discussed, not every physical serving or all vegetables.
Cabbage followed through one preparation. Alternative uses do not assert that one physical serving underwent both alternatives.
Juice belongs to cabbage and may be lost during cooking. No chemical identity, quantity or conserved unit token is given.
Cabbage body distinct from its juice in the causal contrast; not the human body mentioned in4.

reference_inventory.distinction: Retained with cabbage in evacuation branch; poured away in drying branch. No exact amount transferred is written.

reference_inventory.source: ἑτέρῳ θερμῷ / ἐν ἐκείνῳ / εἰς ἐκεῖνο
reference_inventory.distinction: Different water, prepared beforehand and hot, not W1 returned or merely relabeled.
Contains cooked cabbage andwater; not identical with its contents.
Contain prepared oil/fishsauce; plural containers not new independent medicinal plants.
Belly/stomach/gut wording; no specific named modern disease in the two preparation guards.
Exception refers to the whole eye being abnormally moist, not to replacement water.
The prepared lentil dish is not another name for cabbage; similar drying does not imply identical nourishment.
The same name has different referents across speaker communities/times; the contemporary other plant is unnamed here.

uncertainties_and_no_invention: No exact water amount, juice amount, temperature, boiling duration, loss rate or composition balance is given. Numerical mass conservation is not licensed.
The evacuation branch transfers cabbage together with water, but does not say all the water.
The drying branch discards first water and boils in other hot water; this entry does not explicitly instruct discarding the second water before eating. Do not silently add that step.
Air-contact prohibition is written literally alongside cold water. Its practical extent and physical truth are unresolved; it must not be silently rewritten as simply avoiding cooling.
The air/cold-water countercase explicitly predicts failure to soften. It does not separately state the gut effect after that failure; do not invent an additional clinical branch.
The eye exception does not explicitly assert improved vision. The urinary statement is an epistemic limitation, not proven zero effect.
Juice terminology is used for the plant’s own juice and in nutritional humor assessment. No exact modern chemical fraction identity is claimed.
Earlier works/the preceding book are explicitly referenced but not treated as entirely included in this unit. Section3 restates the local transfer dependency.
The contemporary referent of rhaphanos is unnamed here; do not insert a modern species. The600-year contrast is reported authorial speech.
